skills.name: Define relative atomic mass, relative molecular mass, molar mass and molar volume

note.text:
Relative atomic mass (Ar): the average mass of the atoms of an element compared with one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom. It is a ratio, so it has no unit. Ar(H) = 1, Ar(C) = 12, Ar(O) = 16, Ar(Cl) = 35.5.
Relative molecular mass (Mr): the sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule. Mr(H2O) = 2 × 1 + 16 = 18.
For an ionic compound, which has no molecules, the same sum is called the relative formula mass. Mr(NaCl) = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5.
Molar mass: the mass of one mole of a substance, in g/mol. Its number is the same as the relative atomic or molecular mass.
Molar volume: the volume of one mole of ANY gas, 22.4 dm³ at s.t.p. (0 °C and one atmosphere).

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to define and use relative atomic mass, relative molecular mass, molar mass and molar volume.
Builds on: Form Three relative atomic mass and the mole of atoms.
Leads to: Lesson {20} (the mole and the Avogadro constant) and every calculation in this chapter.

sections.heading: Relative masses
sections.text:
Atoms are far too light to weigh one at a time, so their masses are compared with a standard.
RELATIVE ATOMIC MASS (Ar) is the average mass of the atoms of an element compared with one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-{12} atom. Being a ratio, it has no unit: Ar(H) = {1}, Ar(C) = {12}, Ar(O) = {16}, Ar(Cl) = {35.5}.
RELATIVE MOLECULAR MASS (Mr) adds the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule:
{formula('H2O')} = {2} × {1} + {16} = {18}; {formula('H2SO4')} = {2} + {32} + {64} = {98}.
An ionic compound has no molecules, so the same sum is called the RELATIVE FORMULA MASS: {formula('NaCl')} = {23} + {35.5} = {58.5}.

sections.heading: Molar mass and molar volume
sections.text:
MOLAR MASS is the mass of one mole, in grams per mole. Its number is the same as the relative atomic or molecular mass, so one mole of water is {18} g and one mole of carbon dioxide is {44} g.
MOLAR VOLUME is the volume of one mole of any GAS: {22.4} dm³ at s.t.p., which means {0} °C and one atmosphere.
That the same volume holds a mole of any gas follows from Avogadro's law: equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure hold equal numbers of molecules. In a gas the molecules are so far apart that their own size and mass hardly matter.

key_words.meaning: the mass of an atom compared with one twelfth of a carbon-{12} atom
the sum of the relative atomic masses in a molecule
the mass of one mole, in g/mol
{22.4} dm³/mol, the volume of one mole of any gas at s.t.p.
standard temperature and pressure: {0} °C and one atmosphere

examples: {1} mol of any gas = {22.4} dm³ at s.t.p.

mistake.wrong: relative atomic mass is measured in grams
mistake.right: it has no unit at all
mistake.why: It is a RATIO of two masses, so the units cancel. The molar mass, in g/mol, is the one with a unit.

worked_example.problem: Find the relative molecular mass of {formula(F)} and state its molar mass.
steps: Add the relative atomic masses: H is {ram('H')}, S is {ram('S')} and O is {ram('O')}.
The molar mass is the same number with the unit g/mol.
worked_example.answer: relative molecular mass {molarMass(F)}; molar mass {molarMass(F)} g/mol

cards.idea: Relative atomic mass compares an atom with one twelfth of a carbon-{12} atom; it has no unit.
Relative molecular mass is the sum of the relative atomic masses in the formula.
Molar mass is in g/mol; molar volume is {22.4} dm³/mol for any gas at s.t.p.
example: {1} mol of {formula('CO2')} is {44} g and fills {22.4} dm³ at s.t.p.

pick.q: What is the relative atomic mass of an element?
pick.r: The average mass of its atoms compared with one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom
w: The mass of one atom in grams
The number of protons in an atom
The mass of one mole in kilograms
e: The mass of a single atom in grams is far too small to be convenient; a RELATIVE mass is used.
The number of protons is the atomic number, not the mass.
The molar mass is in grams per mole, and relative atomic mass has no unit.
pick.y: It is a ratio, so it has no unit: the relative atomic mass of carbon is {12} exactly.

pick.q: What is the relative molecular mass of a compound?
pick.r: The sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in its molecule
w: The mass of one molecule in grams
The number of atoms in the molecule
The mass of one mole of its atoms
e: Again, a relative mass is used, not the tiny mass in grams.
The number of atoms is a count, not a mass.
That would be the molar mass of the element, not of the compound.

pick.q: Why is 'relative formula mass' used for sodium chloride rather than 'relative molecular mass'?
pick.r: Sodium chloride is ionic, so it has no molecules, only a lattice of ions
w: The two terms mean exactly the same thing
e: Size is not the point; an ionic solid has no separate molecules at all.
It certainly has mass; the point is what the formula stands for.
'Molecular' is used where molecules exist; 'formula' covers ionic compounds too.
pick.y: {formula('NaCl')} is the simplest ratio of ions in the lattice, so the mass found from it is a formula mass.

pick.r: The mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole
w: The number of particles in one mole
The volume of one mole of a gas
e: The number of particles is the Avogadro constant.
That is the molar volume, {22.4} dm³/mol at s.t.p.
The mass of one atom is a tiny number of grams.
pick.y: The molar mass in g/mol is the same number as the relative atomic or molecular mass.

pick.r: The volume occupied by one mole of any gas, {22.4} dm³ at s.t.p.
w: The volume of one mole of any liquid
The volume of one gram of a gas
The volume of {6.02} × {10} to the power {23} atoms of a solid
e: Liquids and solids have very different molar volumes; the rule holds for gases.
The molar volume is per MOLE, not per gram.
The rule applies to gases, not to solids.
pick.y: At the same temperature and pressure, equal volumes of gases hold equal numbers of molecules.

questions.prompt: Find the relative molecular (or formula) mass of {formula(F)}.

misconceptions.explain: {totalAtoms(F)} is the NUMBER of atoms, not their total mass.
Include every atom, not just the first element.

solution: Add the relative atomic mass of every atom in the formula.

questions.prompt: What is the mass, in grams, of {1} mole of {formula(F)}?

misconceptions.explain: Add the masses of the atoms; do not count them.
{22.4} dm³ is the molar VOLUME of a gas, not a mass.

solution: The molar mass in g/mol has the same number as the relative molecular mass.
So {1} mole has a mass of {answer} g.

questions.prompt: What volume, in dm³ at s.t.p., is occupied by {n} mol of {formula(F)} gas?

misconceptions.explain: The question asks for a VOLUME in dm³, not a mass in grams.
Multiply by {22.4} dm³/mol; do not divide.

solution: At s.t.p. {1} mol of any gas fills {22.4} dm³.

pick.q: Two flasks of the same size hold carbon dioxide and hydrogen at the same temperature and pressure. What is the same in both?
pick.y: Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure hold equal numbers of molecules.

pick.q: Why does {1} mol of hydrogen fill the same volume as {1} mol of carbon dioxide at s.t.p., although it is much lighter?
pick.r: The molar volume is the same for every gas: the molecules are far apart whatever their mass
pick.w2: Carbon dioxide molecules are squashed together
pick.w3: They do not fill the same volume
pick.y: In a gas the molecules are so far apart that their own size and mass hardly affect the volume.

pick.q: Which holds more molecules at s.t.p.: {22.4} dm³ of oxygen or {22.4} dm³ of ammonia?
pick.r: Neither: both hold one mole, that is the same number of molecules
pick.w1: The oxygen, because it is denser
pick.w2: The ammonia, because its molecules are smaller
pick.y: Equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure hold equal numbers of molecules.
